title: Flat-preserving colimit functors preserve flat-term K-flat complexes
statement: Let A and B be Grothendieck abelian closed braided monoidal categories with additive tensor [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category], and suppose A has functorial flat resolutions [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution]. Let F:A→B be additive, preserve flat objects and colimits indexed by the ordered integers. If P is K-flat and each P^i is flat, then the degreewise image F(P) is K-flat. K-flat means that tensoring on either side preserves quasi-isomorphisms; flat means that tensoring on either side is exact.

source.place: Tags 064K and 0G7E; flat-resolution, acyclic-cone and good-truncation proof, implemented with the source flat-resolution API.

proof.text: For an acyclic flat-term K-flat complex, tensoring with any object remains acyclic. The flat-opcycles Tor criterion gives flat cycles, using the cycles/opcycles isomorphism of an exact complex. Thus its good upper truncations have flat terms.
The images of these bounded-above flat truncations are K-flat. Their colimit is the image complex, which is K-flat by closure under integer-indexed colimits.

Choose the functorial flat resolution L→P. Its image is K-flat by its bounded-above flat colimit presentation. The cone is acyclic, termwise flat and K-flat. Apply the preceding argument to its image, identify that image with the cone of F(L)→F(P), and use triangulated closure to deduce K-flatness of F(P).
